statement: There are n computers, numbered 0 to n − 1. graph holds the count n and a list of cables [a, b], each directly joining two computers. Computers can reach each other through chains of cables.
In one operation you may unplug any existing cable and use it to join any two computers that were not joined directly.
Return the minimum number of operations needed to make every computer reachable from every other, or −1 if it cannot be done.

examples.explanation: Computers 0, 1 and 2 form a triangle, so one of its three cables is spare. Moving it to computer 3 connects everything.
Connecting 6 computers takes at least 5 cables, and only 3 exist, so it is impossible.
There are three groups, {0, 1, 2}, {3, 4, 5} and {6}. Each triangle has a spare cable, and two moves are enough to join the three groups.

constraints: no two computers are joined by more than one cable
